title: Substantial numerical differences with Minimax MSA attention vs Minimax's Reference
author: CoffeeVampir3

comments.author: Charly21r
comments.body:
Thanks for the analysis, I dug into the code and can confirm this. The bug isn't isolated to that one line, the head-collapse is assumed by every consumer of the selection.

## Root cause
[modular_minimax_m3_vl.py:550](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/minimax_m3_vl/modular_minimax_m3_vl.py#L550):

```
block_scores = scores.amax(dim=-1).amax(dim=1)  # -> [B, S_q, num_key_blocks]
```

scores is `[B, H_idx, S_q, num_key_blocks, block_size]`:
 - `.amax(dim=-1)` pools within the 128-key block
 - .`amax(dim=1)` collapses `H_idx` producing one shared block list per query

The MSA reference's `sparse_topk_select` emits `(total_qo_len, num_qo_heads, topk)` (per-head), where in the MQA-proxy path `max_score.shape[0] == num_kv_heads_real`. With this config `index_n_heads == num_key_value_heads == 4`, so each index head owns one KV group (`qheads_per_kv = 64/4 = 16`). Collapsing the head axis is exactly what drives the ~99.5% selection divergence and the inflated distinct-block count.


It's a shared-selection assumption in 3 places, not one line:
1. Indexer ([modular:550-564](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/minimax_m3_vl/modular_minimax_m3_vl.py#L550-L564)): collapses heads, returns `[B, S_q, topk]`.
2. eager/sdpa mask ([modular:588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/minimax_m3_vl/modular_minimax_m3_vl.py#L588)): build_block_mask does `.unsqueeze(1)`, broadcasting one mask to all query heads.
3. MSA kernel path ([msa_attention.py:204](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/integrations/msa_attention.py#L204)): `q2k ... .unsqueeze(0).expand(num_kv_heads, -1, -1)` literally broadcasts the same list to every KV head instead of indexing per head.

So even the kernel path feeds the deployment kernel a head-broadcast selection.

## Proposed fix
 Keep the head axis end-to-end (index head <-> KV head, 1:1):
- `Indexer.forward`: drop `.amax(dim=1)`, keep `block_scores = [B, H_idx, S_q, num_key_blocks]`, and apply the local-block boost and topk per head -> return `[B, H_idx, S_q, topk]`.
- `build_block_mask`: scatter per index head and `repeat_interleave(num_q_heads // H_idx, dim=1)` so it returns `[B, num_q_heads, S_q, S_k]`.
- `_sparse_attention`: replace the `expand(num_kv_heads, …)` with a real per-head reshape, e.g. `q2k = block_indices.permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(num_kv_heads, bsz * q_len, topk)`.

Plus an equivalence test against the reference selection (the overlap metric above is a good basis).

I'm happy to open a PR for this.
